title: the ugly mind, in the context of reality
content:
I’ve lately been drawing a lot of circles. 

Some satiating dousing falls upon my shoulders and trickles to my fingers when the tip of my graphite briefs that page and travels in a near-perfect rotation of 360 degrees, only slightly oblong by the proper human eye. 

And I’ve been picking at the thought of these wonderful and terribly foolish figures for the past few weeks. Stored safely in the leafed maze of my mind lies a small girl running, only she never stops, just slows and speeds. Within a finite confinement this claim must be a contradiction, unless she crosses over two positions twice, in which case she runs in some sort of a cycle. 

Truly, the issue with the circle lies in its deadly repetition. 

Of course, her movement is purely arbitrary and occurring in free space, sans the infiltration of any external forces that may shift her to follow certain patterns or grid lines. It seems, though, that no matter if she allows her eyelids to rest at 12:00 o’clock or 6:00 o’clock, she decidedly chooses to run over the same path over, and over, sometimes so many times in a row she appears, even from the lowly-educated eye— well, idiotic. 

A child runs into a glass door, falls over, gets up, and then runs into it again. Only a small wail externalizes this time around. 

The larger-than-life caricature residing both inside as well as breaching the boundaries of my physical confinement releases a manic, mocking tune at my current predicament. I look back at him in disbelief. As if I hold the power to harness this idiotic girl running circles within me! We have had this exchange before, I know, and yet I still am bewildered at his audacity to infringe upon actions outside my realm of control. 

Meanwhile, she still runs, and I allow my eyes to drift to watch her. I guess she is quite fascinating. Her movements are hasty scribbles that envelope and intertwine; they exchange conversations that at times so easily fall apart, and at other times hold onto each other as if one strand may seep through and leave the other at any given moment. And then there is a familiar, sticky warmth that spreads throughout me as she continues. She is wild and free, rampant and contagious, animalistic and greatly nondeterministic. And I; well, I am utterly awestruck. 

A child walks onto a balcony, peers over the edge, and jumps over the edge. He receives a large bump on the side of his skull. 

He who I have deemed, “The Introspect,” who is not actually a he, but rather gender non-conforming (I only refer to him as he due to the inadvertent acceptance of my role in gender inequality), he unfortunately yields his eyes in my direction, and although I do not peer toward him, they emblaze a darkened circle (ironic?) into my backside. 

And it is then, when a fire burns in my core, the head inside my head bangs into a wall, again, and again, except with complete determinism this time. 

My pencil lifts from the page that is covered with the terrible creature, and the Introspect rumbles loudly. I slump in my seat and continue. Today we learn about Finitely-Generated Abeleian groups, and a special group that does not run within its grid lines: Monstrous Moonshine.

title: in haste and knowledge
content:
It is my blunder to believe you could fly.

A day existed when I saw you in white. A veil over your eyes, monotonous fabric shrouding the length of your hair, I could not relate to you the color of your skin because there was not a shade I could see. You were beautiful— you are beautiful, I must correct— and yet my eyes never met yours.

When a girl meets a boy, she may see the lilted ovals that sit on the upper third of his face. If his head floats above the rest, she may first stumble into the mounds his neck rests upon and drag her gaze north or south, and upon profiling each section, she may find infinite subsections, some that may pique her interest, and some that may not. Her face may wrinkle at the mouth, or the corners of her almonds, or the bridge of her nose. And as judgement surpasses visibility, the two begin to wield their lips through air and cause bubbles to form, alit with laughter as they sail through the sky. She saw him, and she met him.

Because the day that used to exist, when you wore white and my attention could not stray from your frame, I saw wings. You were brilliant and white particles oblivious to gravity; weight but a negligible quantity to every equation written in your description. Pieces of you that teased the crackled heart over my mouth, whiskers that used to grow from my eyelids, and roses that once bloomed over my bones, my sole flames turned to ice by your touch. In the sky, you were everywhere. Your embrace was a shield against all existent color. You were dense in my thoughts, and you were— are, I must correct— beautiful.

So you spoke to me, and you told me,

“I can,”

And I believed you could.

When a girl lives with a boy, she may observe how he rises with or without the sun. If his head sits over his peers, she may be overjoyed with trinkets, the first few arriving with words unwritten and an intangible yet mobile warmth pervading to her toes. Then there may exist temporary fragments of time when she and him share a smile, his, self-inflicted, and hers, dependent. She may, also, realize tendencies that cause her to widen her jaw, and strain her vocal cords, while his own grow tired from more use than energy to continue. After some hours, or days, or years, limbs caught in limbs, the silent screeching of their mutual exhaust, they still lie together. She lived with him, and she loved him.

I saw you fly. I swear! I saw you fly! Feathers on your back, you leaped and you floated— A threat to all weather, the snow could not suffice as your competitor, Mother Nature, your inferior prodige, you transcended every of my five senses. You flew! And when your feet lifted from the ground, I succumbed to your bewitched kinetics; the fire that I was, the fire that you put out, a new fire grew back within me, twice, thrice as strong. You paraded through my young heart, and my mind cowered in awe. Flames in my gut, my pupils elevated watching you through the sky. My chin raised. I looked up.

When a girl leaves a boy, she may recall the two near-identical paintings she viewed at every moonfall and sunset. Mirrored orbs she first profiled soon revealed more nuance than trite fire and ice: running water and boiling vapor, simmering heat sprinting down to her heart— a quiver and a crack and then, a simple, steady beating. She may replay his strings in her ears, each octave he strung, as her keys danced in rhetoric response. A familiar wind, and an old chime, they interweave their chords as if second nature, until they cannot unfold a new pattern to play.

A veil over your eyes, a brilliant, white day, and you in the center of it all, because I believed you were. The day I took your hand and lifted my eyes to yours, I see clearly now. The first snowfall. Are you beautiful? I ask, because I wonder if your beauty was True, or simply innocence embellished in ice. I saw only white.

I met your eyes. I learned each and every of your physical notches. I sat in your mind and listened, a pen in my hand and a notebook on my knees. Maybe only in the reflection of my own eyes, you flew.

In haste and knowledge, I write, the snow fell. Flowers are blooming.

title: a reflection on autonomous kinematics
content:
I used to believe I was able to move. 

Because I could twist my little fingers, and when a warmth bubbled in my belly, I could lift my lips, and, sometimes, when hands that were not my own danced on my little feet, I let out a yellow rumble, a pink yelp, and bared all my teeth. 

With no restrictions to my kinesthetic sense, I placed one foot in front of the other at any speed I pleased. Sometimes I walked, and sometimes I ran; I crawled, and sometimes I jumped. Sometimes, I reached my giddy arms up to grab at the sky, let my eyelids collapse and my mouth fall ajar, my voice bellowing loud even amidst strays of unkempt judgment. I played in my movement, climbed and swung and slid down every nuance. 

When I was free, and the sun and I used to run to each other, my pupils glazed over with gold and my legs never stopped their oscillation; my lips refused to yield their height and my arms harnessed endless vigor storming against the wind. The moments we met, though my limbs ceased, my chest heaved still. My hands easily flit around myself and my lips fell with no weight, not nearly to horizontal, but rather curved so daintily toward the mirage of color above: the expression of tranquility over exhilarated pandemonium. 
…
I used to believe I was able to move. 

I cannot rotate my head to look into a shard of glass. In isolation my lips are incapable to upturn or bloom downwards, a thin substance falls from my eyes and I struggle to wipe it away because some part of me has grown parasitic upon distorted, misshapen vision. 

I hear heavy metal in my brain; eons of words rage inside of me, feasting among every nimble prey, all incompetent polymorphisms of rationality. A whip—
                                                     thrash—
                                                     menacing, repeated collisions—
emphatically ruminating along my skull and I reach my arms up in an attempt to quell the chaos but my arms do not follow. I place one foot in front of the other but my heels do not lift. I reach my hands forward and back but I cannot sense any motion in my peripheral lens. The sun has set and only charcoal melts over my pupils. 

Every abstraction yells and screams, stomps and shakes me with terror while my physical form holds stationary in the midst of it all.

I want to open my mouth and deplete my lungs, “I CANNOT MOVE,” but I am not equipped with energy for audible speech. My mouth does not open and my lungs remain filled with air. 

Because I cannot twist my little fingers, and when cold burns up in my stomach, my lips do not rise or fall, and sometimes, when hands that are not my own reach out for me, I am unable to formulate any response, only releasing a pitiful plea of a cobalt stare and a gray mumble;

I no longer believe I am able to move.

title: audacity
content:
You asked me how it feels. Every day since then, I’ve let the fragmented memories settle in my sober hours, trying to dissect every moment of my most alluring haze. 

I fiddled with the idea of a brilliant red. Bold and audacious, my internal voices run dry, escaping far beyond their typical filter. 

Or maybe it is the tasting of orange, a burst of citrus infiltrating each layer of my body before settling in my stomach, brimming my insides with a joy not even happiness, excitement, or pure, unscathed and jolly cheer can completely suffice as description. 

I have even thought it as ambling through grays and blacks, where I shiver and my skin turns the stain of spilt sangria, their tips lacking any semblance of heat, comfort, and company. 

However, I’ve realized the effect is the same that used to harbor the scars on my fingers. When warm liquid cascades into the exposed crevices, the cuts on my small limbs leak with puss. They burn and they ache with a pain that travels from my hands to my entire body. 

In the moments I am not myself, when I am not responsible for the rational or moral, and the world around me is not filled with the hard-set, categorical colors of the rainbow, I am simply and breathtakingly White. 

Truthfully, a singular color could never satisfy the requirements of your inquiry, nor see fit to my verbose illustration. I am instead every shade of every color simultaneously, all exploding within me, culminating together into a realm that appears to be lacking all tangible substance or detail. 

There exists a connotation that White is innocent, the earliest form of all Man, uncontaminated by all inevitable, carnal knowledge and resulting sins. But how can it be? White is the pinnacle of Sin; the most beauty is the greatest magnitude of emotion, when violence ensues, sharp clangs of swords rattle as Love, Disappointment, and failed Pride mar together. War, it is War in my body, my mind, and my soul; but a wonderful war, an ethereal war, a war of emotion and passion and pain, one I feel in my darkest trenches, during my most gilding feats or guilty misconducts—

I am Alive. 

The next morning, as my eyes follow the ruin, the permanence of chaos pounds into my skull, and bizarrely— I want it all again. I yearn for thunder; I salivate for the euphoric and ruthless action; I am unsatiated without any notion of sublime dysfunction. Only with my most torturous hurt am I able to relive these moments because during this intense bloodshed— when I sink my teeth into my skin to bring viscous scarlet to my lips or drown my wounds with salt water, when I am, effortlessly, WHITE— I experience all that is, feeling.
